data_quality_notes: RESEARCH COMPLETE — the research phase finished and ran its own verification pass, so nothing here is truncated. What this report is, stated rather than disguised: it is a POSITION-MANAGEMENT report. All 17 ideas concern the existing 19-position book or its 7 unfilled orders, and ZERO new ideas were opened. That was deliberate, not a shortfall — with 19 positions open, a 13% hit rate across 23 closed trades, the rates correlation cap already at 2 of 3, and three positions found to be failing their stop-distance floor, the honest use of the budget was fixing the book rather than adding to it. ACTIONS A READER MUST TAKE TODAY: close CEG, close KHC, close SNX; raise the XLE stop 60.80 -> 65.40; widen the FCX stop 63.35 -> 62.90; stand down on AAL; wait on ABT until after tomorrow's 10/21 print; HII target cut 430 -> 340; BCC conviction cut to 2 and size to 1%. The other eight are holds. TWO IDEAS ARE PUBLISHED BELOW THEIR REWARD-TO-RISK FLOOR and are flagged rather than fixed by nudging a number: FCX at 1.94 against the 2.0 swing floor (after widening the stop to a compliant 2.03 ATR) and HII at 2.44 against the 2.5 long-term floor (after cutting an undefended target). Both are filled positions where the published instruction is risk-reducing — a stop correction and a target cut — so they are carried here so the correction reaches the position record and the red team, not because they clear the bar. Demotion to the watchlist by enforcement is the correct outcome if it takes them. RATIO CLUSTERING, disclosed because it is the signature the pipeline exists to catch: seven of the ten ideas carrying a ratio land between 2.00 and 2.19 against a 2.0 swing floor. The mitigating fact, independently computed, is that every one of those stops clears its ATR floor with room (2.12-3.72 ATR), so the ratios are tight against the floor because the stops are honestly wide, which is the opposite of targets fitted to pass. The stop audit is the run's highest-value finding: recomputing every open position's stop against today's ATR14 caught three failures no amount of news reading would have surfaced — CEG at 1.29 ATR, SNX at 1.80, FCX at 1.86 — and in two of the three the published ratio was clearing 2.0 only because the stop was too tight. CEG and SNX could not be rescued by an honest re-cut (1.66 and 1.86 respectively) and are therefore closes. IYR passes by 0.08 ATR, the thinnest cushion in the book, and that is named in its own key_risk. All three long-term positions (PFE, HII, BCC) were carrying NO priced downside, which strategy.md makes mandatory; anchors were supplied from measured 120-day lows. That is a real weakness and is reported as such: a measured range low is an honest floor but it is closer to a technical level than to the defended valuation the config asks for, which is why PFE and HII are held at conviction 3 rather than the mechanically supported 4. Two of the three also carried targets above every published analyst target — HII's 430 was 26% above the most bullish located (TD Cowen 340) and BCC's 110 is 29% above the highest (Goldman 85), so HII's target was cut to 340 and BCC was cut to conviction 2 at 1% with its target flagged UNVERIFIED. Against a defensible ~88 target BCC's ratio is ~1.0 and it would not qualify at all. Building defended valuations for these is the highest-value item for the next run. FOUR CONVICTIONS SIT BELOW their mechanically supported score and every deviation is downward — nothing was inflated: AAL 2 (the entry is a cancellation, not a position), BCC 2, HII 3, PFE 3. GE and LULU are deliberately held at 3. Conviction 3 is where the track record's damage is concentrated (1/14, avg -6.5%) and conviction 2 is 0/6 at -8.4%, so both conviction-2 entries are sized at or below 1%. PRICES: every quote in this report is the 2026-10-19 close, confirmed re-fetched at 06:35 ET and 875 minutes old in the pre-market session — that is a closed market, not stale data. Two timing caveats matter. GE reports Q3 BEFORE THE OPEN TODAY, so this report is published into that print and no level in the GE entry survives the reaction. STLD already reported after Monday's close ($5.26 diluted EPS vs $5.42 consensus, a headline miss on record shipments) and NO post-print price was obtainable from any source, so its hold is stated explicitly against a pre-print quote. COVERAGE GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES: no index, VIX, rates, DXY, gold or oil quote came from our own feed — every Yahoo-backed series returned HTTP 429 at 06:01 ET, so all macro figures above are web-sourced with URLs and three supporting pages were snippet-only (HTTP 403). The fetched earnings calendar is INCOMPLETE — it does not carry GE, FCX, NEM, NUE, HII, BCC, SNX, DG, LULU or XLF at any horizon tested, and GE is confirmed by two other sources to report today while being absent from it. The rule applied throughout: presence on that calendar is reliable evidence of a date, absence from it is evidence of nothing. FCX's earnings date could not be pinned at all (five conflicting sources: 10/15, 10/21, 10/22, 10/23, 10/27, none official) and NO date is claimed for it, which means that position may be carrying an unflagged print; the same treatment was applied to HII (10/29 reported) and BCC (11/02 reported). Crypto was rejected rather than guessed: spot fetched (BTC 81,442, ETH 2,383.53, SOL 103.97) but history failed on all five sources, so there is no ATR and no swing structure, and setting levels off a single spot print would be fabrication — an uncovered lane with 0 closed trades. Short interest was unavailable all run (api.nasdaq.com ReadTimeout x4), so days-to-cover is unmeasured and named in the key_risk of LULU and AAL. Options-implied move was unavailable (HTTP 401), so no idea was checked against what options price. market_data.py events is broken — the helper mis-scopes the query and reads retired field names; the Kalshi FOMC probabilities used here were fetched from the API directly and the helper needs a fix plus a test. A short-gold idea was rejected on driver conflict rather than levels: rising real yields is gold-bearish but the same session's Hormuz and Saudi strikes are gold-positive, and it would have been a third idea on the rates driver. Four positions (DG, NKE, XLF, CVS) were reviewed, passed the stop audit, had no new information in the window, and were deliberately NOT re-pitched — re-publishing a position with nothing new is padding. Not reached: small and micro-cap hunting. RED TEAM (phase 2c, 17 ideas reviewed, 1 cut, 4 convictions lowered, 1 stated probability withdrawn, nothing raised and no level moved outward). CUT: LULU to the watchlist — its 2.07 reward-to-risk rests entirely on a 77.00 target with no evidence item, no anchor and no method behind it, 7.71 ATR out and 14.8% below a 120-day low that held; re-cut to the only defended level in the idea (90.38) the ratio is 0.90:1. Synthesis caught exactly this defect in HII and BCC and missed it in LULU; this is the consistent treatment, not a new standard. The LULU note is a withdrawal of the recommendation, not an instruction to close the position. CONVICTIONS LOWERED: IYR 5 -> 4 and TLT 5 -> 4, both for the same two reasons — their 'positioning' evidence restates the single 10/19 rate-and-sector move the catalyst and technical_level already carry rather than confirming it independently, and their counter_argument_answered item is rebutted by their own key_risk (the Kalshi ladder prices the policy rate, not the 10-year, the term premium or the statement language). ABT 4 -> 3: its positioning evidence (one beat in four quarters, $46.85M of insider selling against $1.30M of buying) argues against the long, leaving a date and a chart level behind a conviction 4 whose own instruction is 'do not enter'. WITHDRAWN: XLE's stated 45% win probability, set to null rather than re-estimated — it was scored against a 4.40:1 that only exists because the validator measures risk from a 63.90 cost basis the raised 65.40 stop now sits above. The forward ratio is the ~1.1:1 the idea's own counter_argument states, where break-even is ~48%, so the claimed figure was below its break-even rather than 26 points above it; the stop raise is kept and the half-trim at 68.50 is now named as the load-bearing instruction. market_context.summary: Monday 2026-10-19 was a one-factor session and the factor was rates. The 10-year rose 4-6bp to 5.14-5.15% with the 30-year reported near its 2002 highs, and that single move produced the whole sector table: utilities -2.01% and real estate -1.16% were the two worst S&P sectors, with no company-specific story in either. Equities nonetheless rose on a tech-led rebound — S&P 500 7,690.73 (+0.41%), Nasdaq Composite 26,430.89 (+1.11%) — while the Dow slipped 0.07% on JPMorgan. VIX closed 18.44 (-7.75%), but Cboe's own 10/19 digest records VIX having run ~5 points higher week-on-week into Friday on a scramble for downside hedges, with 1-month SPX 30-delta skew jumping from the 15th to the 82nd percentile while MOVE held 99-102: equity hedging demand is already in place with rate vol contained. The second live driver is energy supply — WTI settled $103.66 (+2.22%) and Brent traded ~$110 intraday on Houthi missile strikes on Saudi targets, attacks on shipping near Hormuz and a Ukrainian strike on a Russian refinery, taking XOM, CVX and MPC to 52-week highs. The dated event that governs the next three weeks is the 2026-10-27/28 FOMC, the only meeting before 2026-12-09; Kalshi prices it 86% hold, 13% a 25bp hike and 1% a cut, so the priced tail is hawkish, not dovish.

recommendations.thesis: UPDATE to the open short entered 2026-09-24 at 79.90, now 79.46 — hold, levels unchanged, and the thesis got two independent confirmations. The first is price: the 10-year rose 4-6bp to 5.14-5.15% on 2026-10-19 with the 30-year reported near 2002 highs, and that single move took utilities down 2.01% and real estate down 1.16% as the worst two S&P sectors. TLT closed 79.46, below its 80.67 50-day. The second is the event market, and it is the more useful one: Kalshi contracts on the 2026-10-28 decision price **86% hold, 13% a 25bp hike, and only 1% a cut**, against roughly 1.9M in open interest on the hold leg. The distribution is skewed toward tightening, not easing, which is the opposite of the risk a short-duration position normally carries into a Fed meeting. The calendar compounds it: this is the only meeting before 2026-12-09, so there is no second chance to reprice the front end this side of December. Requires margin — flagged.
recommendations.key_risk: The event market prices the *policy* decision, not the long end, and this position is in 20-year-plus duration where term premium and auction demand drive the price — the Fed can hold exactly as priced and TLT can still rally hard on a weak auction, a growth scare, or a flight to quality. That bid arrives without notice: VIX ran ~5 points higher week-on-week into 2026-10-16 with 1-month SPX 30-delta skew jumping from the 15th to the 82nd percentile, so hedging demand is already in place and an equity air pocket during mega-cap earnings week sends TLT through 82.00 on a day when nothing changed about rates. The 82.00 stop is 2.52 ATR above entry — fine for an ordinary day, no defence against a risk-off gap. Being short also means paying the distribution.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against the short is that it is late and crowded: the 10-year at 5.14-5.15% and the 30-year at 2002 highs is a position the whole market now holds, the 75.70 target sits *below* the 76.43 120-day low so the trade needs new lows rather than continuation, and crowded short-bond positioning is what produces violent squeezes. The squeeze mechanism is now answered with a priced number rather than an opinion: the event market puts a rate cut at the 2026-10-28 meeting at **1%**, so the specific catalyst that would force that squeeze is not merely unlikely in my estimation, it is unlikely in the market own pricing with real money behind it. What remains unanswered is the crowding itself, which is why the add instruction is explicitly closed off after the statement and the half-trim sits at 76.43 rather than at the target. RED TEAM (conviction cut 5 -> 4): the Kalshi ladder was independently re-fetched at 06:45 ET and verified (1c/13c/87c/1c/1c, 1,941,905 open interest on the hold leg), so the evidence is real — but it is doing more work than it can bear in two ways. First, this idea's 'positioning' evidence is half a restatement of the same 10/19 rate move the technical_level already carries, and its other half — the Cboe skew and MOVE reading — is reproduced verbatim in key_risk as the mechanism by which this short loses money. Evidence that argues against the trade cannot also pay for conviction in it. Second, the counter_argument states outright that the crowding objection remains unanswered, and crowding is the primary risk in a short-duration trade the whole market is already in. A conviction 5 with its strongest objection conceded is a 4. The reward-to-risk also sits at exactly 2.00 against a 2.00 floor, so there is no margin anywhere in this idea. Levels, stop and the no-add-after-the-statement instruction all stand.

recommendations.thesis: UPDATE to the unfilled ABT idea published 2026-10-16 at 103.0 — the level is unchanged but the instruction is now WAIT, and that is the whole recommendation. The new fact is that Q3 earnings land 2026-10-21 before the open, one session away, and the fetched surprise record says ABT has beaten consensus in only **one of its last four quarters** (+1.38% in Q2 after -0.45%, -0.75% and -1.06%). With spot at 104.06 and the limit at 103.0, the single most likely way this pullback entry ever fills is the earnings gap itself — which is the mechanism that selects for exactly the ideas that were already failing. Sell-side has gone the other way into the print: 81.2% bullish of 32 analysts with zero sells, up 9.8 points since July. Analysts raising the bar on a company that keeps missing it by a hair is a reason to let the print clear first, not to pre-position for it.
recommendations.key_risk: Waiting means giving up the gap-up: if ABT finally beats and guides up, it re-rates toward the 105.80 50-day and beyond without ever touching 103, and the idea is never entered at all — the same outcome it has had since 2026-10-16. The entry risk being avoided is the mirror image: a 2.36 ATR stock that gaps 5% on a guidance change fills the 103 limit on the way to 96, below the 98.0 stop, so the stop is not protection against this particular event.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for leaving the limit live is that the four misses are tiny — the largest is 1.06%, which is noise in a $13B quarter and says more about how tightly ABT guides the street than about the business, and a company that lands within 1% of consensus every time is precisely the one you can safely pre-position in. Answered with the price record rather than asserted away: ABT is 11.32% off its 117.34 range high and still 26.95% above an 81.97 range low set inside the same 120 bars, so this name has in fact made large moves this year, and the 101.03 20-day sitting 2.9% under spot with the 105.80 50-day 1.7% above it is a stock with no established trend to lean on through an event. RED TEAM (conviction cut 4 -> 3): the analysis here is right and the WAIT instruction is kept intact, but the score is not paid for. The 'positioning' evidence — beats in one of the last four quarters, and $46.85M of insider selling against $1.30M of buying whose most recent purchase is five months old and 17% below spot — argues against a long, not for one. Strip it and the direction is supported by a fetched earnings date and a chart level, with the idea's own thesis describing a stock with no established trend to lean on through an event. A conviction 4 on an idea whose published instruction is 'do not enter' overstates it; 3 is the honest score for standing down.
